ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 3 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Flannery O'Connor — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Kidney biopsy result: class III lupus nephritis; start of pulse methylprednisolone, prednisone, mycophenolate, and belimumab

text.paragraph: Kidney biopsy result and start of treatment. [S]

Ms. O'Connor had an ultrasound-guided kidney biopsy five days ago without bleeding. It shows ISN/RPS class III (A) lupus nephritis: focal endocapillary proliferation in 9 of 30 glomeruli, activity index 6 of 24, chronicity index 1 of 12, with no crescents or thrombotic microangiopathy. She heard the result from Dr. Okonjo-Strand by telephone two days ago, as she had asked, and again in full today. A levonorgestrel intrauterine system was inserted yesterday. Her joints and rash are unchanged; she has taken hydroxychloroquine and losartan for a week. Today she has the first of three methylprednisolone infusions, starts mycophenolate, and learns to give herself belimumab. She asked how to keep her mornings for writing through treatment. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1950-04-29; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Biopsy site clean and healing; no tenderness
Synovitis of the hands and wrists as before; full painless hip movement

Pain and swelling of the small joints of both hands, the wrists, and the knees for three months, with an hour of morning stiffness, evening fevers to 38 °C, fatigue, and a red rash over the cheeks and nose after sun; told elsewhere it might be rheumatoid arthritis; cause to be established

S — Synthetic presenting concern at the index visit, superseded by the diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus at the second visit; joint pain in 1950 with suspected rheumatoid arthritis is documented (D).
Protein and blood in the urine: protein-to-creatinine ratio 1.6 g/g and 18 red cells per high-power field, with normal creatinine; cause to be established
S — Synthetic presenting finding at the index visit, superseded by the kidney biopsy diagnosis at the third visit.

Systemic lupus erythematosus, classified by the EULAR/ACR criteria (ANA 1:640 homogeneous; score 32 before the biopsy): inflammatory arthritis, acute cutaneous lupus (malar rash), fever, leukopenia with lymphopenia, mild thrombocytopenia, low C3 and C4, anti-dsDNA and anti-Sm positive; antiphospholipid antibodies and lupus anticoagulant negative
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis and results; her systemic lupus erythematosus, diagnosed in Atlanta in late 1950 or early 1951, is documented (D), but no finding from her lifetime is used.

S — Synthetic biopsy result and class; kidney involvement is documented at the end of her life, but no kidney finding from her lifetime is used.
Long-term glucocorticoid treatment for lupus nephritis, tapering to 5 mg a day or less
S — Synthetic treatment status; the documented steroid harm in her life is the reason the episode keeps glucocorticoids low.

list.item:
Class III lupus nephritis (M32.14). Active focal proliferative lupus nephritis with little chronic damage and normal kidney function, so the outlook with treatment is good. Treatment follows the current ACR lupus nephritis guideline: pulse glucocorticoids, then an oral taper, with two other immunosuppressive drugs. She chose mycophenolate with belimumab, given by her own weekly injection at home, rather than mycophenolate with voclosporin, which needs closer kidney and blood pressure monitoring. The goal is a protein-to-creatinine ratio below 0.5 g/g within a year. [S]
Methylprednisolone 500 mg intravenously today and the next two days.
Then prednisone 30 mg daily, reduced by 5 mg every two weeks to 10 mg, then to 5 mg or less by six months.
Mycophenolate 500 mg twice daily for a week, then 1000 mg twice daily; blood counts weekly for the first month, twice monthly for the next two, then monthly.
Belimumab 400 mg weekly for four doses, then 200 mg weekly, by self-injection; report low mood.
Pneumocystis prophylaxis discussed and not started, because the prednisone dose falls below 20 mg within six weeks and sulfonamides are avoided in lupus; reconsider if the dose stays high.

Glucocorticoid treatment: bone and avascular necrosis (Z79.52). DXA Z-scores -0.4 at the spine and -0.2 at the femoral neck are normal for age, and with no fracture her fracture risk is low, so no osteoporosis drug is needed; vitamin D is low at 26. High-dose glucocorticoids carry a risk of avascular necrosis of the hip. [S]
Vitamin D3 1000 units daily and calcium from food.
Report any new hip, groin, or knee pain at once; MRI of the hips if it occurs.
Prednisone taken in the morning; watch glucose, blood pressure, sleep, and mood.

Contraception (Z97.5). Intrauterine system in place; pregnancy test negative; she can start mycophenolate. [S]
Keep the intrauterine system throughout mycophenolate treatment.

list.item: Establish the diagnosis within two weeks and hear it directly, in plain words. Outcome by 1950-04-22: Told directly at nine days that she has systemic lupus erythematosus, with the reasons and a written summary [S]
Renal response: urine protein-to-creatinine ratio halved by three months and below 0.5 g/g with stable kidney function by six to twelve months. In progress; target 1950-10-26 [S]
Prednisone 5 mg a day or less by six months, with withdrawal considered later. In progress; target 1950-10-26 [S]
Write at least four mornings a week through treatment. In progress; target 1950-12-31 [S]
No unplanned pregnancy on mycophenolate; plan any pregnancy for a time of quiet disease on compatible medicines. In progress; target 1950-12-31 [S]

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: EULAR recommendations for the management of systemic lupus erythematosus: 2023 update. Ann Rheum Dis 2024;83(1):15-29 (2023); 2024 American College of Rheumatology (ACR) Guideline for the Screening, Treatment, and Management of Lupus Nephritis. Arthritis Rheumatol 2025;77(9):1115-1135 (2024); 2022 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Prevention and Treatment of Glucocorticoid-Induced Osteoporosis. Arthritis Rheumatol 2023;75(12):2088-2102 (2022); BENLYSTA (belimumab): prescribing information (subcutaneous dosing for lupus nephritis) (2026); CELLCEPT (mycophenolate mofetil): prescribing information (blood count monitoring, embryofetal toxicity, contraception) (2026)

Follow-up: Methylprednisolone tomorrow and the day after. Rheumatology blood counts weekly. Ophthalmology in two months. Three-month review. Next scheduled visit 1950-07-27: three-month response assessment for lupus nephritis and glucocorticoid taper. [S]
